Kurt Alme

Republican candidate for United States Senator, Montana · Open seat

Former U.S. Attorney for the District of Montana; former Montana state budget director

Kurt Alme is the Republican nominee for U.S. Senate in Montana. Incumbent Sen. Steve Daines is not running for a third term, and Alme filed for the seat on March 4, 2026, minutes before the filing deadline. Daines, Gov. Greg Gianforte and President Trump endorsed him, and he won the June 2, 2026 Republican primary.

Where Alme stands

War powers
Says the Constitution gives Congress the power to declare war and that Congress should consistently enforce its role. Also says presidents must be able to act quickly to protect Americans.
Rural health care
Supports building on the Rural Health Transformation Program and investing in providers instead of subsidizing insurers. Backs expanding telehealth and requiring health care price transparency.
Public safety and drugs
Supports border security, backing law enforcement and prosecuting violent criminals and drug trafficking organizations up to the cartels. Proposes more focus on drug prevention and treatment.
Cost of living and housing
Argues that cutting deficit spending and balancing budgets will lower prices. Supports reducing regulations that slow home construction in order to increase housing supply.
Federal spending
Proposes bringing his Montana budget experience to Washington: balancing budgets, cutting spending and providing tax relief.

Background

  • U.S. Attorney for the District of Montana, 2017–2020 (first Trump administration)
  • Montana budget director under Gov. Greg Gianforte, starting in 2021
  • Appointed U.S. Attorney for Montana again in Trump's second term; resigned to run for Senate in 2026
  • Former director, Montana Department of Revenue
  • Former president, Yellowstone Boys & Girls Ranch Foundation
  • Born October 7, 1966, in Great Falls, Montana
  • First run for elected office
